scenes.visual: Terminals card: each agent a separate install, login, bill
scenes.text: AI coding agents are now a real line item. Claude Code, Codex, Qwen Code, MiniMax, Gemini CLI: each is a separate install, login and bill, tied to its own models. And none of them is best at everything.

scenes.visual: Equation card: model + harness = coding agent
scenes.text: That's because an agent is really a model plus a harness: the tools, the prompts and the loop around it. OpenCode made the model swappable. The harness matters just as much.

scenes.visual: New landing page: Every coding agent. One platform.
scenes.text: Meet OpenHarness: a harness and model agnostic coding platform. Think Devin, but you choose the agent. Ten harnesses, sixty-five models, one place and one bill, all running on HarnessRouter.
Pick a repo and a harness: here, Qwen Code. Then the model. Qwen Code alone runs sixty of them, from Qwen and DeepSeek to Claude and GPT. We'll take Qwen 3.8 Max and run the task.
Every command and edit streams in live, while the agent works in an isolated HarnessRouter sandbox. This was seventeen minutes of real work, sped up.
Then you review it like a pull request: summary, tests, the full diff, and the exact cost. Ten new tests, all passing, for a dollar twenty. And follow-ups keep the same session, with full context.

scenes.visual: Side by side setup: Qwen Code vs Codex on gpt-6-luna
scenes.text: Now, the part that saves money. Same task, side by side: Qwen Code on Qwen 3.8 Max, and Codex running GPT-6 Luna.

Codex finished in under five minutes for three cents. Qwen Code took longer and ninety cents, but got every test passing. That's a twenty-seven-x price spread on one task. Send routine work to the cheap agent, and save the premium one for the hard problems.

scenes.visual: Four agents side by side, then Usage & budget
scenes.text: Run up to four agents at once, and see exactly what every harness and model costs you, metered per task. Set a monthly budget, and OpenHarness enforces it.

We built this during the hackathon because HarnessRouter does the heavy lifting: one API for every harness, with sandboxes, sessions and files built in. The next great harness is a config change for us, and zero work for our users.

And it's a real business. Developers pay per task, with our margin on every run, and teams pay for budgets, policies and shared sessions. Next is Auto mode, which picks the best harness and model for each task and budget, learned from the outcomes we already track. Every task we sell is a HarnessRouter task.
OpenHarness. Any harness. Any model. One platform.
